subject.title: Make Codex supervision interactive and owned by the Codex plugin

question: Should the official Codex plugin absorb Gateway-local interactive supervision and shipped codex-supervisor configuration while paired-node rows remain read-only until runner leasing exists?
rationale: Source inspection supports local forking, but plugin ownership, migration compatibility, model-lock invariants, archive confirmation, and remote scope are deliberate product and security choices.

options.title: Phase local consolidation
options.body: Move Gateway-local branching and guarded archive into the official Codex plugin, migrate shipped supervisor configuration through doctor, and keep paired-node rows metadata-only.

options.title: Keep plugins separate
options.body: Retain codex-supervisor as the catalog and mutation owner, accepting duplicate App Server and configuration ownership.

options.title: Defer interaction
options.body: Keep the existing read-only catalog until one local-and-remote runner-ownership protocol is designed.

recommendation.title: Phase local consolidation
recommendation.body: Move Gateway-local branching and guarded archive into the official Codex plugin, migrate shipped supervisor configuration through doctor, and keep paired-node rows metadata-only.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to steipete and their recent merged work established both the catalog foundation and native-thread control surface.
